Third, the subscript g or u describes how the wave function changes as we in- vert our point of observation through the center of the molecule. Imagine Cartesian coordinates with their origin at the center of the molecule, and compare the wave function at the point (x, y, z) and at the point (2x, 2y, 2z). If the sign of the wave function is the same at these two points, it is called symmetric and labeled g for the German word gerade (even). If the sign of the wave function is opposite at these two points, it is called antisymmetric and labeled u, for the German word ungerade
